title: Guardian evaluation layer and authz proxy for API & Console
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a lightweight evaluation layer ("Guardian") and a small authz proxy to centralize RBAC v2 policy evaluation for requests across the public API, runtime ingestion paths, and the Redwood Console. Guardian will: 1) provide a single evaluation abstraction that consumes canonical policies and user/session context, 2) expose a gRPC/HTTP API that the API gateway, runtime frontends, and console can call, and 3) emit enriched audit events to the audit pipeline. The authz proxy is a sidecar-style shim to be deployed with runtime components where embedding the full Guardian client is infeasible.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Guardian evaluates RBAC v2 policies within target latency SLOs for 99th percentile (<= 6ms for cached rules, <= 20ms cold path); 2) API gateway and Console call Guardian for every protected route and reject unauthorized requests with standardized error codes; 3) Sidecar authz proxy implements policy cache with TTL and circuit-breaker fallback to allow degraded operation; 4) All authorization decisions are emitted to the audit pipeline with request_id, principal, decision, policy_version, and attrs; 5) SSO/SAML-derived groups and roles map to RBAC v2 schema and are test-covered; 6) End-to-end tests + canary rollout performed with telemetry in Grafana dashboard.
technical_design: High-level: Guardian is a stateless service that loads policy bundles from the policy-store (s3/kv) and keeps a hot in-memory rule index for fast lookup. Evaluation path: request -> attribute enrichment (from token/session+SAML assertions) -> rule index lookup -> policy decision with allow/deny/conditional attributes -> audit event. Sidecar authz-proxy wraps local components and maintains an LRU cache keyed by (principal, resource, action, policy_version). Key decisions: use protobuf/gRPC for internal calls to minimize serialization overhead; provide HTTP/JSON adapter for the Console; keep policy format compatible with existing policy compiler but introduce a flattened index for performance. Fall-back behavior: if Guardian is unavailable, proxy can consult local cached decisions and, if TTL expired, either fail-open for low-risk routes (metrics only) or fail-closed for admin/privileged routes. Telemetry: per-decision latency histogram, cache hit/miss, policy_version drift metric, and audit event delivery status.
implementation_notes: Sprint plan: Week 1: policy-store adapter + bundle loader; Week 2: rule index and evaluation micro-benchmarks; Week 3: HTTP/gRPC adapters + sidecar; Week 4: audit enrichment and pipeline integration; Week 5: SSO mapping + integration tests; Week 6: canary, observability, and runbook. Performance optimizations: compact rule index to reduce pointer chasing, precompute role-to-perm bitsets for common roles, integrate a hot-path JIT for complex condition checks if profiler indicates. Security: sign/verify policy bundles with KMS; validate SAML assertions against IdP metadata; ensure no PII leaks in audit events (hash sensitive ids). Backwards compatibility: expose a compatibility adapter layer to accept legacy authorizer calls for a transition window. Docs & runbook: update console RBAC docs, add incident runbook for policy-rollbacks.
